title: Universal property of a faithfully flat affine group quotient
statement: Let $F$ be a field [def-weil-field], and let $G,Q,H$ be affine $F$-group schemes [def-sc-group-scheme] of finite type [def-weil-finite-type-morphism]. Let $q:G\to Q$ be a homomorphism such that $q^*:F[Q]\to F[G]$ is faithfully flat, meaning extension of scalars is exact and detects zero modules. Put $N=\ker q$, the scheme-theoretic kernel, and let $i:N\to G$ be its inclusion. For every homomorphism $u:G\to H$ satisfying $u\circ i=e_H\circ(N\to\operatorname{Spec}F)$, there is a unique homomorphism $v:Q\to H$ with $u=v\circ q$. The equality on $N$ is an equality of group-scheme morphisms, equivalently on points over every commutative $F$-algebra, and is not merely equality on $F$-points. No smoothness or connectedness assumption is made.

source.place: Theorem 5.13, printed p.101, with quotient-map hypothesis supplied by Definition 5.5 and Proposition 5.43, printed pp.99,107: faithfully flat affine group homomorphisms are quotient maps.

proof.text: Write $A=F[Q]$ and $B=F[G]$. By the affine-spectrum correspondence, $q$ is the spectrum of $q^*:A\to B$. Faithful flatness includes flatness; the affine flatness criterion therefore makes $q$ flat, and faithfully flat surjectivity on spectra makes $q$ surjective.

The singleton $\{q\}$ is an fpqc covering. Indeed, for any affine open $V\subset Q$, choose principal opens $D(a)\subset V$ covering it, using the principal-open basis on $\operatorname{Spec}A$. Quasi-compactness of the affine scheme $V$ gives finitely many $D(a_1),\ldots,D(a_r)$ covering $V$. Their inverse images are the principal opens $D(q^*a_j)$ of the affine scheme $G$, hence are affine by clause (0) of the affine-open localization statement. Surjectivity of $q$ says their images cover $V$. Together with flatness from step 1, this is exactly the defining finite-affine-open condition for an fpqc covering.

source.place: Tag 022B (definition-fpqc-covering), checked directly; affine basic opens and quasi-compactness: algebra.tex Tags 00E0, 00E8; schemes.tex affine structure sheaf on principal opens.

proof.text: Put $P=G\times_QG$ with projections $p_1,p_2$. All maps are over $F$. Define $d:P\to G$ by $d=p_1^{-1}p_2$, using the inverse and multiplication morphisms of $G$. Since $q$ is a homomorphism and $qp_1=qp_2$, one has $qd=e_Q\circ(P\to\operatorname{Spec}F)$. The universal property of the kernel fibre product therefore gives $a:P\to N$ with $ia=d$. The assumption $ui=e_H$ gives $ud=e_H$. Applying $u$ to $p_2=p_1d$ now yields $up_2=(up_1)(ud)=up_1$. These are identities of scheme morphisms, obtained from group-object diagrams and the kernel universal property.

source.place: Theorem 5.13, printed p.101: kernel triviality makes the homomorphism constant on kernel cosets; here expressed on the kernel pair.

proof.text: Apply representable fpqc descent to the cover $q:G\to Q$ of step 2 and the compatible morphism $u:G\to H$ of step 3. It gives a unique scheme morphism $v:Q\to H$ with $vq=u$. It is over $F$: the two maps $Q\to\operatorname{Spec}F$ given by the structure map and by $v$ followed by the structure map of $H$ agree after $q$, since $u$ is over $F$; the uniqueness assertion of the same descent statement makes them equal.

source.place: Tag 023Q (lemma-fpqc-universal-effective-epimorphisms), existence and uniqueness; this spells out the descent assertion used in Milne Theorem 5.13.

proof.text: By base change and composition of fpqc coverings, $q\times_Fq:G\times_FG\to Q\times_FQ$ is an fpqc covering: factor it as $G\times_FG\to Q\times_FG\to Q\times_FQ$, each factor a base change of $q$. The two $F$-morphisms $v\circ m_Q$ and $m_H\circ(v\times_Fv)$ agree after this cover, because their composites are respectively $u\circ m_G$ and $m_H\circ(u\times_Fu)$, equal since $u$ is a homomorphism. Uniqueness in representable fpqc descent makes them equal on $Q\times_FQ$. Thus $v$ preserves multiplication, which is the definition of a group-scheme homomorphism. Every other required homomorphism is also a scheme morphism factoring $u$, so equals $v$ by step 4.

source.place: Tag 023Q, uniqueness, with topologies.tex Tag 022D (lemma-fpqc), parts (2) and (3); Milne Theorem 5.13, final homomorphism assertion.
